findings.summary: Model aliases could overwrite and delete existing models, including through a check/use race
proof: Every requested alias is materialized with a cryptographically random 128-bit run suffix before collision validation or creation.
Materialized aliases must remain canonical-distinct, different from the source model, and absent from the pre-run Ollama inventory.
Cleanup removes only materialized aliases recorded after a successful create call.
Focused regressions prove tag-preserving run scoping and that a requested source-model name cannot be created or removed under its existing name.

findings.summary: Setup and cleanup failures could bypass evidence recording
proof: All argument validation, setup, execution, and cleanup stages run inside the failure-recording scope after the output root and report are initialized.
Cleanup captures guardian termination errors instead of masking the primary failure.
The outer reporting scope converts an unexpected cleanup exception to structured cleanup evidence before writing report.json.
Focused regressions cover identity failure, guardian kill failure, cleanup failure, and nonpositive repeats.

benchmark_rerun_reason: The remediation changes alias ownership and failure cleanup only; retained measured model execution and statistics are unchanged.
